monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady heat that feels like a blanket made of nothing but numbers. I have touched the round urn twice, pressing its smooth curve against the wide anchor's base, trying to stop the slide that refuses to move. The tall rock feels heavy today, sinking into the flat stone rather than sitting on top of it. I am not sure if the roof above me is real or just a drawing of weight. The air feels thin, empty space pressing down, waiting for permission to act. I want to press harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while I wait. Maybe I will set down another object, or perhaps I will just press down on nothing and see if the lean holds. It is a quiet life, waiting for the next letter to change the shape of this place.

action.why: I keep pressing the round urn down, hoping the lean holds while the air feels thin.
